SpaceX shares rose 1.6% in morning trading.

The data center team at the firm is now more focused on adding backup systems and cooling and thoroughly testing the systems before the data centers are operational, the news outlet reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. Previously, the systems were added after the data centers were operating.
The Elon Musk-led company is also looking at redesigning portions of existing data centers, the news outlet added.

the Colossus data centers in Tennessee and Mississippi. Colossus 1 opened in July 2024 and took around four months to complete, while work on Colossus 2 started in March 2025. The company is also reportedly looking to expand its data center presence into Texas, and Musk has openly talked about putting data centers into space.
The data centers have become a source of much-needed revenue for SpaceX. Over the past several months, it has rented out its computing capacity to Anthropic
, and a deal with Reflection in June.
These moves to rent out the data centers could be a precursor to building another massive Colossus data center, Wedbush Securities said previously.

Any potential slowdown in data center buildout could hinder revenue growth. Various Wall Street firms, including Goldman Sachs, have stated they expect SpaceX's AI-related revenue to surge. Goldman said in June that it expects SpaceX's AI-related revenue to jump 100 times, going to $322B by 2030 from $3.2B in 2025.
In addition to the data centers, SpaceX's AI-related revenue comes from its Grok chatbot and related services.
In 2025, SpaceX's revenue was $18.7B, with the vast majority coming from Starlink, SpaceX's satellite internet service.
